topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer development through mutation and clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can drive clonal evolution within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and their contribution relative to chance and inheritance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk alongside intrinsic mutation processes and inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can contribute to carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma developing the general account into a detailed example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage from environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage, showing how their effects depend on chemical activation and the conditions of exposure.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require subsequent tumour-promoting conditions for cancer to develop.

topics.label: Context-dependent carcinogen susceptibility and mechanistic synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete the mechanistic account by explaining context-dependent susceptibility and consolidating the preceding explanations of carcinogen action.

topics.label: Evidence and methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic effects can be investigated and how the limitations of available evidence constrain causal conclusions.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing consolidates the lecture's conclusions and frames their practical implications as decisions about risks and benefits.
